entries.content_osis: <div eID="gen56085" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s">Introduction</title> <div sID="gen56086" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen56087" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen56087" type="x-p"/> <div eID="gen56086" type="introduction"/> <div sID="gen56088" type="x-p"/> The four angels holding the four winds of heaven, <reference osisRef="Rev.7.1">Rev 7:1</reference>. The angel with the seal of the living God, and sealing the servants of God out of the twelve tribes, whose number amounted to one hundred and forty-four thousand, <reference osisRef="Rev.7.2-Rev.7.8">Rev 7:2-8</reference>. Besides these, there was an innumerable multitude from all nations, who gave glory to God and the Lamb, <reference osisRef="Rev.7.9-Rev.7.12">Rev 7:9-12</reference>. One of the elders shows who these are, and describes their most happy state, <reference osisRef="Rev.7.13-Rev.7.17">Rev 7:13-17</reference>. <div eID="gen56088" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56089" type="x-p"/> <hi type="bold">Verse 1</hi> <div eID="gen56089" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56090" type="x-p"/> And after these things - Immediately after the preceding vision. <div eID="gen56090" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56091" type="x-p"/> I saw four angels - Instruments which God employs in the dispensation of his providence; we know not what. <div eID="gen56091" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56092" type="x-p"/> On the four corners of the earth - On the extreme parts of the land of Judea, called ἡ γη, the land, or earth, by way of eminence. <div eID="gen56092" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56093" type="x-p"/> Holding the four winds - Preventing evil from every quarter. Earth - sea, nor on any tree; keeping the whole of the land free from evil, till the Church of Christ should wax strong, and each of his followers have time to prepare for his flight from Jerusalem, previously to its total destruction by the Romans.
entries.content_plain: Introduction The four angels holding the four winds of heaven, Rev 7:1 . The angel with the seal of the living God, and sealing the servants of God out of the twelve tribes, whose number amounted to one hundred and forty-four thousand, Rev 7:2-8 . Besides these, there was an innumerable multitude from all nations, who gave glory to God and the Lamb, Rev 7:9-12 . One of the elders shows who these are, and describes their most happy state, Rev 7:13-17 . Verse 1 And after these things - Immediately after the preceding vision. I saw four angels - Instruments which God employs in the dispensation of his providence; we know not what. On the four corners of the earth - On the extreme parts of the land of Judea, called ἡ γη, the land, or earth, by way of eminence. Holding the four winds - Preventing evil from every quarter. Earth - sea, nor on any tree; keeping the whole of the land free from evil, till the Church of Christ should wax strong, and each of his followers have time to prepare for his flight from Jerusalem, previously to its total destruction by the Romans.

Some understand this of Christ, who is called ανατολη, the east, <reference osisRef="Luk.1.78">Luk 1:78</reference>. <div eID="gen56094" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56095" type="x-p"/> Four angels, to whom it was given to hurt - Particular agents employed by Divine providence in the management of the affairs of the earth; but whether spiritual or material we know not.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 3</hi> <div eID="gen56095" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56096" type="x-p"/> Till we have sealed the servants of our God - There is manifestly an allusion to <reference osisRef="Eze.9.4">Eze 9:4</reference> here. By sealing we are to understand consecrating the persons in a more especial manner to God, and showing, by this mark of God upon them, that they were under his more immediate protection, and that nothing should hurt them. It was a custom in the east, and indeed in the west too, to stamp with a hot iron the name of the owner upon the forehead or shoulder of his slave. <div eID="gen56096" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56097" type="x-p"/> It is worthy of remark that not one Christian perished in the siege of Jerusalem; all had left the city, and escaped to Pella. This I have often had occasion to notice.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 4</hi> <div eID="gen56097" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56098" type="x-p"/> I heard the number of them which were sealed - In the number of 144,000 are included all the Jews converted to Christianity; 12,000 out of each of the twelve tribes: but this must be only a certain for an uncertain number; for it is not to be supposed that just 12,000 were converted out of each of the twelve tribes.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen56098" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56099" type="x-p"/> Of the tribe of Juda, etc. - First, we are to observe that the tribe of Levi is here mentioned, though that tribe had no inheritance in Israel; but they now belonged to the spiritual priesthood. Secondly, That the tribe of Dan, which had an inheritance, is here omitted; as also the tribe of Ephraim. Thirdly, That the tribe of Joseph is here added in the place of Ephraim. Ephraim and Dan, being the principal promoters of idolatry, are left out in this enumeration.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 17</hi> <div eID="gen56116" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56117" type="x-p"/> The Lamb - The Lord Jesus, enthroned with his Father in ineffable glory. <div eID="gen56117" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56118" type="x-p"/> Shall feed them - Shall communicate to them every thing calculated to secure, continue, and increase their happiness. <div eID="gen56118" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56119" type="x-p"/> Living fountains of water - A spring in the Hebrew phraseology is termed living water, because constantly boiling up and running on. By these perpetual fountains we are to understand endless sources of comfort and happiness, which Jesus Christ will open out of his own infinite plenitude to all glorified souls. These eternal living fountains will make an infinite variety in the enjoyments of the blessed. There will be no sameness, and consequently no cloying with the perpetual enjoyment of the same things; every moment will open a new source of pleasure, instruction, and improvement; they shall make an eternal progression into the fullness of God. And as God is infinite, so his attributes are infinite; and throughout infinity more and more of those attributes will be discovered; and the discovery of each will be a new fountain or source of pleasure and enjoyment. These sources must be opening through all eternity, and yet, through all eternity, there will still remain, in the absolute perfections of the Godhead, an infinity of them to be opened! This is one of the finest images in the Bible. <div eID="gen56119" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen56120" type="x-p"/> God shall wipe away - In the most affectionate and fatherly manner, all tears from their eyes - all causes of distress and grief. They shall have pure, unmixed happiness. Reader, this is the happiness of those who are washed from their sins. Art thou washed? entries.content_plain: Verse 17 The Lamb - The Lord Jesus, enthroned with his Father in ineffable glory. Shall feed them - Shall communicate to them every thing calculated to secure, continue, and increase their happiness. Living fountains of water - A spring in the Hebrew phraseology is termed living water, because constantly boiling up and running on. By these perpetual fountains we are to understand endless sources of comfort and happiness, which Jesus Christ will open out of his own infinite plenitude to all glorified souls. These eternal living fountains will make an infinite variety in the enjoyments of the blessed. There will be no sameness, and consequently no cloying with the perpetual enjoyment of the same things; every moment will open a new source of pleasure, instruction, and improvement; they shall make an eternal progression into the fullness of God. And as God is infinite, so his attributes are infinite; and throughout infinity more and more of those attributes will be discovered; and the discovery of each will be a new fountain or source of pleasure and enjoyment. These sources must be opening through all eternity, and yet, through all eternity, there will still remain, in the absolute perfections of the Godhead, an infinity of them to be opened! This is one of the finest images in the Bible. God shall wipe away - In the most affectionate and fatherly manner, all tears from their eyes - all causes of distress and grief. navigation_sections.title: Revelation · Original Chapter 7 Introduction
navigation_sections.content_plain: Introduction The four angels holding the four winds of heaven, Rev 7:1 . The angel with the seal of the living God, and sealing the servants of God out of the twelve tribes, whose number amounted to one hundred and forty-four thousand, Rev 7:2-8 . Besides these, there was an innumerable multitude from all nations, who gave glory to God and the Lamb, Rev 7:9-12 . One of the elders shows who these are, and describes their most happy state, Rev 7:13-17 .
